The principal question is: does the GeminiSupervisor machine that exists today actually contain and enforce everything the user still wants today, and if not, exactly what surviving requirements are missing, partial, unenforced, or incorrectly represented? Independently choose and state the historical interpretation heuristic you believe best solves that problem, while obeying the fixed transport and context architecture. Historical facts, semantic interpretations, and truth decisions must remain distinct, and truth decisions that depend on historical meaning must explicitly identify the interpretations on which they depend. Requirement lifecycle and implementation state are independent where useful: an implemented or unimplemented historical requirement may later be superseded; superseded requirements do not create present corrective work. Detect partial as well as full supersession. Establish today's actual machine behavior from executable source, workflows, configuration, persisted structures, and deterministic behavior; specification text and historical model self-report do not alone prove implementation. Recover the surviving desired requirements from the historical evidence, account for every relevant historical instruction, and compare every surviving requirement against the current machine. Use the precomputed deterministic segment inventory and the supplied segmentation policy. The lead planner receives segment metadata only and must group every segment into exactly one primary batch plus justified crosscheck batches. Primary batches must cover 100% of raw context without duplication. Crosschecks may overlap, redistribute, or use seeded stochastic selection when justified, but primary plus crosscheck raw context must never exceed 1.5 times one complete raw corpus pass. All policy batch-size ceilings are hard limits. Every primary batch and every crosscheck batch must be evaluated by a freshly instantiated evaluator process that receives only that one batch's raw context plus the common task/schema; it must receive no previous batch conversation, no previous raw context, and no previous batch result. Do not use recursive Gemini calls, model-directed compute loops, or whole-audit retries. After all isolated batch results exist, synthesize them through a fixed fresh-process reduction tree: balance the serialized compact batch results into four approximately equal result-volume groups Q1-Q4; synthesize each quarter independently; synthesize Q1+Q2 into D1 and Q3+Q4 into D2; then perform one final synthesis from D1+D2 only. No raw historical evidence may be reintroduced after the batch layer. Preserve provenance, contradictions, indeterminate cases, requirement lineage, implementation findings, and completeness accounting through every synthesis stage. Return the final historical_audit_result with a verified description of the machine today, surviving requirements, superseded requirements, outstanding gaps, historical facts, interpretations, truth_decisions, crosscheck reconciliation, completeness checks, unresolved ambiguities, and provenance.
